item: Small cocycle with a prescribed word value (paper lem:small-cocycle, cocycle.tex:31-46; Lean OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.smallCocycle)
item_statement: For n>=3 and eta>0 there are a word w in F_n and a finitely supported real h with ||h||_2 < eta such that the 1-cocycle D into l2(F_n) (left regular action) with D_{x_1}=h, D_{x_j}=0 (j>=2) satisfies ||D_w - delta_e||_2 < eta.
lean_status_why: smallCocycle states exactly lem:small-cocycle (n>=3, one word, coefficients on the first generator only, both l2 bounds < eta) and uses the paper's prefix words p_j = (a b_1)...(a b_j), b_j = x_2^j x_3 x_2^-j, but it solves the inverse problem T_m h ~ delta_e by an explicit alternating, Cesaro-averaged radial series on F_m (Radial.averagedInverse) instead of the paper's Catalan-moment / free-Poisson spectral limit and cutoff inverse.
lean_gaps: Proof route of the analytic core differs. Paper: lem:cocycle-spectrum (mu_m -> density (1/2pi)sqrt((4-x)/x) on (0,4), no atom at 0) plus a spectral cutoff inverse. Lean: Radial.partialInverse (alternating sum of normalized odd shells), Radial.averagedInverse (Cesaro mean), with exact identities sqNorm_partialInverse = N/m and sqNorm_averagedInverse_residual = (m-1)/(m(N+1)); then m >> N. No spectral theory, no free probability.

Freeness of the prefixes: paper uses a reduced-word argument plus the Nielsen pair phi/psi; Lean uses a semidirect-product witness FreeGroup Z x| Z and a telescoping left inverse (PrefixSeparation.prefixHom_injective). Same conclusion.
Statement: identical up to 0-indexing (generator 0 = x_1) and Coeff G = G ->0 R (finitely supported reals, as in the paper). No hypothesis added or dropped.

IMPORTANT for the tests: in Lean the headline instance L(F_2) = L(F_3) does NOT use smallCocycle. finiteRank_to_two 3 uses rankTwo = rank_step_ge_two 2, which goes through one_step_two -> smallCocycleTwo (RankTwoCoefficients.lean:543), a Lean-only rank-two variant (~1.8k lines, RankTwoCoefficients/Words/Counting) that reuses the Radial shells with approximately free prefixes. smallCocycle (n>=3) is used by rankStep (L(F_n)=L(F_n+1), n>=3) and by rankThreeInfinite (via FiniteActive.one_step), and hence by the infinite and non-integer models of the comparator. The paper instead has n>=3 only and gets n=2 from Dykema's formula. Any hide-the-item experiment must hide smallCocycle, smallCocycleTwo and the Radial file together.

Interface: Lean factors the absorption step as one_step_of_coefficient_estimate (FiniteRank.lean:15), which takes the small-cocycle property as a hypothesis hc for any n. This gives a clean device -> consequence boundary for a speedup test.

Comparator is stronger than the paper's headline (all r,s in (1,infinity]), but non-integer L(F_r) is DEFINED by Dykema's corner formula (trusted definition); the fundamental-group claim is proved (allInterpolatedFundamentalGroups) but not compared; family 287 has no formalization.yaml entry.
Generation step (not part of this item) uses Baire category in Lean versus an explicit adaptive iteration in the paper.

argument: The item as a library STATEMENT is route-independent: smallCocycle is verbatim lem:small-cocycle, so adding the statement to L is the same under either route.

If the device's INTERNALS are added (the arm that tests reuse of the construction, not just the lemma), only the Lean route is usable: Radial.exists_small_prefix_inverse is a self-contained, group-only statement about l2(F_m) ('delta_e has an approximate preimage of norm sqrt((N+1)/m) under 1 + sum_i lambda(x_i)'), with explicit vectors (shells) that other proofs can reuse. The paper's route needs weak convergence of spectral measures of non-normal operators, the free CLT / Marchenko-Pastur law and Borel functional calculus cutoffs, none of which exist in Mathlib d13f23b (needs a major new library).

The Lean route shows that once the problem is posed, solving it is elementary (about 800 lines of combinatorics on spheres of F_m). So the eureka content sits in posing the coupled problem (small generator coefficient, prescribed word value, fed to the absorption flow), and the speedup test should give the prover the statement plus the one_step_of_coefficient_estimate interface, not the paper's spectral proof.

Use three arms: (A) baseline L; (B) L + smallCocycle statement; (C) L + smallCocycle + Radial.exists_small_prefix_inverse + PrefixSeparation.prefixHom_injective + cocycle_push_prefix_inverse. Arm C measures reuse of the construction; arm B measures reuse of the lemma.
The paper version remains the reference for discoverability (test 4) judging: a model output matching either proof counts as a hit.

comparator_chain: [infinity and continuous r] Model.toRankTwo -> rankTwo.trans rankThreeInfinite (FreeGroupFactor/Main.lean:56) -> InfiniteGeneration.rank_three_to_index -> one_step_none -> FiniteActive.one_step (FreeGroupFactor/FiniteActive.lean:388) -> smallCocycle; continuous r also via rankTwo_allPositiveScaling (InterpolatedFactors/Positive.lean:122), which uses rankTwo.trans rankThreeInfinite
[n=2,3 only] rankTwo (FiniteRank.lean:147) -> rank_step_ge_two -> one_step_ge_two (FiniteRank.lean:42) -> one_step_two -> smallCocycleTwo (RankTwoCoefficients.lean:543), bypassing smallCocycle
comparator_dependency_verdict: The comparator theorem depends on smallCocycle (knockout breaks rankStep, rankThreeInfinite, hence integer models n>=4, the infinite model and every non-integer model). The specific instance L(F_2)=L(F_3) does not depend on it in Lean (it uses smallCocycleTwo).

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.smallCocycle
lean_source.text:
theorem smallCocycle (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) :
    ∃ (w : FreeGroup (Fin n)) (h : Coeff (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      coefficientNorm h < η ∧
        coefficientNorm (freeCocycle (firstCoefficients h) w - Finsupp.single 1 1) < η

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.coefficientNorm
lean_source.text:
def coefficientNorm {G : Type uG} (h : Coeff G) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (h.sum (fun _ r => r ^ 2))

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.firstCoefficients
lean_source.text:
def firstCoefficients {n : ℕ} (h : Coeff (FreeGroup (Fin n))) :
    Fin n → Coeff (FreeGroup (Fin n)) := fun i => if i.val = 0 then h else 0

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.sourceB
OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.sourcePrefix
OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.sourceWord
lean_source.text:
def sourceWord (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (m : ℕ) : FreeGroup (Fin n) :=
  sourcePrefix n hn m * sourceA n hn

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.Coeff
lean_source.text: abbrev Coeff (G : Type uG) := G →₀ ℝ

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.freeCocycle
lean_source.text:
def freeCocycle {ι : Type uι} (h : ι → Coeff (FreeGroup ι)) (g : FreeGroup ι) :
    Coeff (FreeGroup ι) := (cocycleGraph h g).left.toAdd

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.freeCocycle_mul
lean_source.text:
theorem freeCocycle_mul {ι : Type uι} (h : ι → Coeff (FreeGroup ι)) (g b : FreeGroup ι) :
    freeCocycle h (g * b) = freeCocycle h g + coefficientShift g (freeCocycle h b)

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.PrefixSeparation.prefixHom_injective
lean_source.text:
theorem prefixHom_injective (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (m : ℕ) :
    Function.Injective (prefixHom n hn m)

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.PrefixSeparation.prefixHom
lean_source.text:
def prefixHom (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (m : ℕ) : FreeGroup (Fin m) →* FreeGroup (Fin n) :=
  FreeGroup.lift (fun i => sourcePrefix n hn (i.val + 1))

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.cocycle_push_prefix_inverse
lean_source.text:
theorem cocycle_push_prefix_inverse (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (m : ℕ)
    (h : FreeGroup (Fin m) →₀ ℝ) :
    freeCocycle (firstCoefficients (pushCoefficients (PrefixSeparation.prefixHom n hn m) h))
        (sourceWord n hn m) =
      pushCoefficients (PrefixSeparation.prefixHom n hn m) (Radial.prefixSumOperator m h)

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.Radial.sumShift
lean_source.text:
def sumShift : (FreeGroup ι →₀ ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] (FreeGroup ι →₀ ℝ) :=
  ∑ i : ι, shift (FreeGroup.of i)

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.Radial.sumShift_shell_succ
lean_source.text:
theorem sumShift_shell_succ [Nonempty ι] (k : ℕ) :
    sumShift (shell (ι := ι) false (k + 2)) =
      ((Fintype.card ι - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) • shell (ι := ι) true (k + 1) +
        shell (ι := ι) true (k + 3)

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.Radial.rightShell
lean_source.text:
def rightShell (m k : ℕ) : FreeGroup (Fin m) →₀ ℝ :=
  (1 / ((m : ℝ) * ((m : ℝ) - 1) ^ k)) • shell false (2 * k + 1)

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.Radial.partialInverse
lean_source.text:
def partialInverse (m N : ℕ) : FreeGroup (Fin m) →₀ ℝ :=
  ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, (-1 : ℝ) ^ k • rightShell m k

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.Radial.averagedInverse
lean_source.text:
def averagedInverse (m N : ℕ) : FreeGroup (Fin m) →₀ ℝ :=
  (1 / (N + 1 : ℝ)) • ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), partialInverse m (k + 1)

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.Radial.sqNorm_averagedInverse_residual
lean_source.text:
theorem sqNorm_averagedInverse_residual (m N : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) :
    coefficientSqNorm (sumShift (averagedInverse m N) - Finsupp.single 1 1) =
      ((m : ℝ) - 1) / ((m : ℝ) * (N + 1 : ℝ))

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.Radial.prefixSumOperator
lean_source.text:
def prefixSumOperator (m : ℕ) (h : FreeGroup (Fin m) →₀ ℝ) : FreeGroup (Fin m) →₀ ℝ :=
  h + sumShift h

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.Radial.exists_small_prefix_inverse
lean_source.text:
theorem exists_small_prefix_inverse (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ m : ℕ, 2 ≤ m ∧ ∃ h : FreeGroup (Fin m) →₀ ℝ,
      coefficientSqNorm h < ε ∧
        coefficientSqNorm (prefixSumOperator m h - Finsupp.single 1 1) < ε

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.one_step_of_coefficient_estimate
lean_source.text:
theorem one_step_of_coefficient_estimate (n : ℕ)
    (hc : ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ (w : FreeGroup (Fin n)) (h : Coeff (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      coefficientNorm h < η ∧
        coefficientNorm (freeCocycle (firstCoefficients h) w-Finsupp.single 1 1) < η) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ α : groupVonNeumann (FreeGroup (Option (Fin n))) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] groupVonNeumann (FreeGroup (Option (Fin n))),
      (∀ T, canonicalTrace (α T) = canonicalTrace T) ∧
      @Continuous _ _ (groupUltraweakTopology (FreeGroup (Option (Fin n))))
        (groupUltraweakTopology (FreeGroup (Option (Fin n)))) α ∧
      ∃ w : FreeGroup (Fin n),
        (∀ j : Fin n, ‖α (groupUnitary (FreeGroup.of (some j))) - groupUnitary (FreeGroup.of (some j))‖ < ε) ∧
        twoNorm (α (groupUnitary (FreeGroup.map Option.some w)) - groupUnitary (FreeGroup.of none)) < ε

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.one_step
lean_source.text:
theorem one_step (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ α : groupVonNeumann (FreeGroup (Option (Fin n))) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] groupVonNeumann (FreeGroup (Option (Fin n))),
      (∀ T, canonicalTrace (α T) = canonicalTrace T) ∧
      @Continuous _ _ (groupUltraweakTopology (FreeGroup (Option (Fin n))))
        (groupUltraweakTopology (FreeGroup (Option (Fin n)))) α ∧
      ∃ w : FreeGroup (Fin n),
        (∀ j : Fin n, ‖α (groupUnitary (FreeGroup.of (some j))) - groupUnitary (FreeGroup.of (some j))‖ < ε) ∧
        twoNorm (α (groupUnitary (FreeGroup.map Option.some w)) - groupUnitary (FreeGroup.of none)) < ε

lean_source.name: OAI.FreeGroupFactorMain.smallCocycleTwo
lean_source.text:
theorem smallCocycleTwo (η : ℝ) (hη : 0 < η) :
    ∃ (w : FreeGroup (Fin 2)) (h : Coeff (FreeGroup (Fin 2))),
      coefficientNorm h < η ∧
        coefficientNorm (freeCocycle (firstCoefficients h) w-Finsupp.single 1 1) < η

lean_source.text:
theorem allInterpolatedIsomorphic (r s : ℝ≥0∞) (hr : 1<r) (hs : 1<s) :
    Nonempty (NormalTracialEquiv (interpolatedTrace r) (interpolatedTrace s)
      (interpolatedTopology r) (interpolatedTopology s))

speedup_targets.title: Rank-two small cocycle (smallCocycleTwo)
speedup_targets.statement: For every eta>0 there are w in F_2 and finitely supported real h with ||h||_2<eta and ||D_w - delta_e||_2 < eta, where D_{x_1}=h, D_{x_2}=0.
speedup_targets.reference: OAI Lean, FreeGroupFactor/RankTwoCoefficients.lean:543 (Lean-only; not in the paper, which assumes n>=3)
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Lean: RankTwoCoefficients 577 + RankTwoWords 489 + RankTwoCounting 742 = 1,808 lines (on top of the shared Radial file, 571 lines). Paper: none (n=2 obtained via Dykema).
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: The n>=3 proof cannot be transported directly: with only two generators, D vanishes only on <x_2> = Z and the obvious prefixes x_1 x_2^j are not free (u_1 u_2^-1 u_3 = u_2). The rank-two proof pushes the same Radial shells through an almost-injective prefix map (prefixHom B m) and bounds overlap errors. With smallCocycle, exists_small_prefix_inverse and the push lemmas in L, the remaining work is the near-freeness counting; a prover should find the shell-pushing plan much faster.
speedup_targets.caveat: In-family sibling, not an independent theorem: useful to calibrate the speedup harness, weak as confirmation of a jump.

speedup_targets.title: Free absorption over a base containing a free pair (device reuse beyond the theorem)
speedup_targets.statement: If a countable group Gamma contains two elements s,t generating a free subgroup, then L(Gamma * Z) = L(Gamma * F_2) (normal, trace-preserving), e.g. Gamma = SL(3,Z).
speedup_targets.reference: New (suggested here). Related: Dykema 1993 (Duke Math. J. 69) and Dykema-Radulescu 2000 (Math. Ann.) on free products Q * L(F_r); status of the r=1 case for non-free-product Q not verified.
speedup_targets.status: not known to us; treat as new until checked against Dykema-Radulescu
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: This is NOT a corollary of L(F_2)=L(F_3) (functoriality of free products gives Q*L(F_2)=Q*L(F_3), not Q*L(Z)=Q*L(F_2)). The device seems to run unchanged: let u generate Z, take b_j = s^j t s^-j in Gamma, prefixes p_j = (u b_1)...(u b_j) free in Gamma*Z; the cocycle with D_u = h, D|Gamma = 0 is well defined on the free product; T_m h ~ delta_e is exactly exists_small_prefix_inverse pushed along p; the flow moves u only and fixes L(Gamma) (as FiniteActive.one_step fixes its kappa generators); the Nielsen correction C -> C u_w fixes Gamma; Baire generation then gives W*(L(Gamma), u') = L(Gamma * Z * Z_C) with u' Haar and free from L(Gamma).
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: high (if true, the proof is a re-parametrization of the 287 Lean; without the item a prover has no route)

speedup_targets.title: Akemann-Ostrand lower bound via radial shells (sub-device control)
speedup_targets.statement: For the m free generators x_i of F_m, ||sum_{i=1}^m lambda(x_i)|| >= 2 sqrt(m-1) on l2(F_m) (equality is Akemann-Ostrand).
speedup_targets.reference: C. A. Akemann, P. A. Ostrand, 'Computing norms in group C*-algebras', Amer. J. Math. 98 (1976) 1015-1047
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: about 2-4 pages for the norm formula; no Lean formalization found (Mathlib has none).
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Radial.sumShift_shell_succ gives S r_{k+1} = sqrt(m-1)(l_k + l_{k+1}) on normalized odd/even shells (from sumShift_rightShell_succ and the shell norms), a bidiagonal Jacobi matrix whose norm tends to 2 sqrt(m-1). The lower bound is then a short computation with test vectors sum_k c_k r_k.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: med for the lower bound; none for the upper bound
speedup_targets.caveat: Measures the classical radial-shell sub-device (Haagerup/Pytlik-type, N0), not the small-cocycle statement. Use it as a control that separates infrastructure reuse from item reuse.

speedup_targets.title: Generator problem perturbation (family 296, Prop. 'perturbation with uniform correlation')
speedup_targets.statement: For an irreducible inclusion P in M of II_1 factors, unitaries u,z in M, xi in M, 0<alpha<1/2 and every l>=1, there are u~ with ||u~-u||_2 <= alpha/sqrt(2l)+1/l and t_0..t_l in U(P) such that the word W = t_0 prod (u~ t_k) has |tau(xi* W) - (alpha/2) tau(xi* z)| <= ||xi||_2 4alpha^2/(1-2alpha) + 1/l.
speedup_targets.status: proved in the release (unrefereed); Lean in OAI/Analysis/FactorGeneration (33.1k lines in total)
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: paper about 4 pages; Lean perturbation layer (PerturbationBounds, WordCorrelation, Convolution, Exponential and related files) is a few thousand lines inside FactorGeneration
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: The first-order term of the perturbed word is a Fox-cocycle value along free prefixes, the same structure as D_w = T_m h. 287's lemma would give a prescribed VALUE where 296 only needs a positive correlation, so the linear part is easier in 296, not harder. The hard parts of 296 (nonlinear remainder via Haagerup's length-one inequality; Popa's free independence in ultrapowers) are untouched.

speedup_targets.title: Surface-group factors (Shlyakhtenko 2026, Thm 3/4)
speedup_targets.statement: L(pi_1 Sigma_g) = L(F_{2g-1}) for g>=2; technical form: for every eta there is a Haar unitary v with ||v-A||_2<eta and L(F_2) = W*([A,B]) * W*(v).
speedup_targets.reference: D. Shlyakhtenko, 'On the II_1 factors of Fuchsian groups', arXiv:2609.11074v1 (2026-09-10; declared ChatGPT Pro 6.0-assisted), https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11074
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Weakly. 287 absorbs an extra generator that is FREE from the moved tuple; here the target B is not free from (A,[A,B]), and a relation-compatible cocycle (one that vanishes on the relator) is needed. The prefix-sum inverse could supply the amplification step that Shlyakhtenko's Lemma 9 does with exp(i sqrt(t/2m)(z+zbar)) multipliers.

speedup_targets.title: Non-vanishing of l2 first cohomology of F_n (ceiling check)
speedup_targets.statement: There is no C with ||b(g)|| <= C max_j ||b(x_j)|| for all l2(F_n)-valued 1-cocycles b and all g; equivalently (F_n non-amenable) H^1(F_n, l2 F_n) != 0, beta_1^(2)(F_n) > 0, F_n lacks property (T).

open_problems.title: Free absorption L(Gamma*Z) = L(Gamma*F_2) for groups containing F_2
open_problems.statement: See speedup target 2. More generally: for which ICC groups Gamma is L(Gamma) = L(Gamma * Z)?
open_problems.reference: Posed here as a device test. Background: Dykema, Duke Math. J. 69 (1993); Dykema-Radulescu, Math. Ann. (2000); Popa (property (T) obstruction).
open_problems.status: open as far as found (not checked against the Dykema-Radulescu literature)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Exactly the 287 obstruction: absorb one extra free Haar generator by small automorphisms. The ingredients the device needs (a free prefix family for the moved generator, a cocycle vanishing off that generator) exist whenever Gamma contains a free pair.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Replace x_2, x_3 by s, t in Gamma; define the cocycle on Gamma * <u>; run one_step with Gamma fixed; Baire-generate. Known failures bound the scope: if L(Gamma) has property (T) then L(Gamma) != L(Gamma*Z) (free products are never (T)), so the question is about Gamma*Z versus Gamma*F_2, not Gamma versus Gamma*Z.
open_problems.payoff: med-high (a free absorption theorem for arbitrary bases, beyond what the isomorphism theorem gives)

open_problems.title: de la Harpe-Voiculescu conjecture for Fuchsian groups with torsion
open_problems.statement: For a cocompact Fuchsian group Gamma with torsion (e.g. hyperbolic triangle groups Delta(p,q,r)), is L(Gamma) an interpolated free group factor (now: is L(Gamma) = L(F_2))?
open_problems.reference: Shlyakhtenko, arXiv:2609.11074 Sec. 1 (settles the torsion-free case; states the torsion cases are not all settled); conjecture attributed there to de la Harpe and Voiculescu
open_problems.status: open in the torsion cases not covered by Shlyakhtenko's Theorem 1 (as reported by the summariser; verify)
open_problems.obstruction_match: beta_1^(2)(Gamma) = -chi(Gamma) > 0 supplies l2 cocycles, as for F_n; but generators of finite order are not Haar and relators force the cocycle to vanish on them, so 287's 'coefficients on one generator' choice fails.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Work in Gamma * Z or in a finite-index free/surface subgroup; build a relation-compatible prescribed-value cocycle; combine with Shlyakhtenko's free-complement theorem and 287's full fundamental group to pass to finite-index overgroups.

open_problems.title: Is L-infinity(U_N^+) (free unitary quantum group, N>=3) a free group factor?
open_problems.statement: Is the von Neumann algebra of Wang's free unitary quantum group U_N^+ isomorphic to L(F_2)?
open_problems.reference: Brannan-Vergnioux, 'Orthogonal free quantum group factors are strongly 1-bounded', Adv. Math. (2018), arXiv:1703.08134 (settles O_N^+ negatively, leaves U_N^+); Kyed-Raum-Vaes-Valvekens, Anal. PDE 10 (2017) (beta_1^(2) of the dual of U_N^+ equals 1)
open_problems.status: open as far as found (search 2026-10-09; index stale for 2026)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Positive first L2-Betti number (the precondition for small cocycles) holds, unlike O_N^+; Banica's free complexification puts L-infinity(U_N^+) inside L(Z) * L-infinity(O_N^+), which supplies a Haar unitary free from a large subalgebra.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Quantum analogue of the prefix family and the prescribed-value cocycle in the quantum Cayley tree; drive a flow by it; absorb a free Haar generator; then use 287's isomorphism theorem.

missing: compact quantum groups, Haar state, free quantum group C*-algebras (thousands of lines)

open_problems.title: q-Gaussian factors versus free group factors for large |q|
open_problems.statement: Is Gamma_q(R^N) = L(F_N) (equivalently, after 287, = L(F_2)) for all q in (-1,1)?
open_problems.reference: Guionnet-Shlyakhtenko, 'Free monotone transport', Invent. Math. 197 (2014) (proves it for |q| < q(N))
open_problems.obstruction_match: Fox derivative = free difference quotient; Gamma_q has closable derivations with good regularity (conjugate variables), the noncommutative replacement for l2 cocycles.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Replace the group cocycle by a derivation into the coarse bimodule with a prescribed value; drive 287's flow by it; needs a free Haar extra generator, which Gamma_q does not provide directly.
open_problems.payoff: med (the small-|q| case is known; large |q| would be new)

missing: Fock space with q-deformed inner product, q-Gaussian algebra (est. 1-3k lines; OAI FreeEntropy has some free Fock tooling)

open_problems.title: Free Araki-Woods factors: multiplicity of the continuous part
open_problems.statement: Is the free Araki-Woods factor Gamma(mu) determined by the measure class of mu alone, i.e. is Gamma(mu) = Gamma(mu + mu') when mu' is absolutely continuous with respect to mu (type III analogue of absorbing a free generator)?
open_problems.reference: Shlyakhtenko, 'Free quasi-free states', Pacific J. Math. 177 (1997); Houdayer's structural papers on free Araki-Woods factors (2007-2010)
open_problems.status: open as far as we know (not re-verified in this session)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Same as 287's (multiplicity versus isomorphism), but for non-atomic mu the centralizer is trivial, so there are no Haar unitaries in the centralizer for the tracial flow to move.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Replace the trace by the free quasi-free state, the cocycle by a modular-covariant one, and the flow by a state-preserving one. The trivial centralizer is a likely blocker.

missing: free quasi-free states, modular theory (OAI ModularTheory exists but no free Araki-Woods)

theorem_corollaries: All interpolated free group factors L(F_r), 1<r<=infinity, are isomorphic (the comparator).
Fundamental group of L(F_2) is R_{>0} (Lean allInterpolatedFundamentalGroups; not compared).
Free entropy dimensions (delta_0, delta*, ...) and beta_1^(2) are not W*-invariants: each integer value n>=2 is attained on generating tuples of L(F_2) (287 Cor. 7.1, cited by family 296).
Every Shlyakhtenko identification L(Gamma) = L(F_r) (torsion-free Fuchsian groups) collapses to L(Gamma) = L(F_2).
Dykema's free products of hyperfinite / finite-dimensional algebras with free dimension > 1 (e.g. L(PSL_2(Z)) = L(F_{7/6})) are all = L(F_2).
Single generation of L(F_n) for all n (also proved independently, for all II_1 factors, by family 296).

L(F_3) = L(F_infinity): classically equivalent to the full isomorphism via the Dykema-Radulescu dichotomy; Lean proves it directly with the device (FiniteActive.one_step -> smallCocycle), which is in-family reuse, not independent evidence.

release_reuse.what: smallCocycle is used twice (LocalAutomorphism.one_step for rankStep; FiniteActive.one_step for rankThreeInfinite). The Radial shells are reused by smallCocycleTwo (RankTwoCoefficients.lean), with an almost-injective prefix map and explicit overlap constants.

Independent design sibling: a perturbation of u of size alpha/sqrt(l) spread over l occurrences in a long word with free coefficients, giving an O(alpha) first-order effect (correlation with a target z), plus Baire genericity. Same amplification-along-free-prefixes design, in correlation form rather than prescribed value. 296's Lean imports FreeGroupFactor.Operators (infrastructure) but not Cocycles/Radial/SmallCocycle (grep over lean/OAI: no file outside FreeGroupFactor uses freeCocycle or exists_small_prefix_inverse).
release_reuse.counts_as_device_reuse: design-level sibling, not reuse of the lemma

release_reuse.where: outside the release: Shlyakhtenko arXiv:2609.11074 Lemma 9
release_reuse.what: sqrt(t/m)-per-step perturbations accumulating to an O(t) effect along BA^-m; same scaling, no cocycle formulation (per novelty.json).

negative_controls.title: Reduced group C*-algebras
negative_controls.statement: C*_r(F_2) and C*_r(F_3) are not isomorphic (K_1 = Z^n).
negative_controls.why: Proved-false analogue. The device must leave the C*-world (S = Arg(C) is a Borel, not continuous, logarithm). Any norm-continuous version of the flow would contradict K-theory; a prover using the item should not 'prove' the C*-version.

negative_controls.title: Orbit equivalence / Cartan pairs
negative_controls.statement: Free p.m.p. actions of F_2 and F_3 are never orbit equivalent; the Cartan pairs (L-inf(X) x| F_n, L-inf(X)) are pairwise non-isomorphic.
negative_controls.why: Proved-false analogue: the device's automorphisms do not preserve a Cartan subalgebra; cost is an invariant.

negative_controls.title: Groups with vanishing first L2-Betti number
negative_controls.statement: For finitely presented sofic Gamma with beta_1^(2)(Gamma)=0 (e.g. F_2 x F_2, BS(2,3), SL(3,Z)), L(Gamma) is strongly 1-bounded, hence not = L(F_2).
negative_controls.reference: Shlyakhtenko, 'Von Neumann algebras of sofic groups with beta_1^(2)=0 are strongly 1-bounded', J. Operator Theory (2021); Jung's strong 1-boundedness
negative_controls.why: The small-cocycle property fails there: for non-amenable Gamma with H^1(Gamma, l2 Gamma)=0 every l2 cocycle is a coboundary with a uniform constant, so ||b(w)|| <= C max_s ||b(s)||. It also fails for Z (Dirichlet kernel zeros).

negative_controls.title: Free orthogonal quantum groups
negative_controls.statement: L-infinity(O_N^+), N>=3, is strongly 1-bounded and not a free group factor.
negative_controls.reference: Brannan-Vergnioux, Adv. Math. (2018), arXiv:1703.08134; Vergnioux (beta_1^(2)=0), Adv. Math. 229 (2012)
negative_controls.why: Quantum analogue with vanishing first L2-Betti number: the device must not apply.

top5.title: Free absorption L(Gamma*Z) = L(Gamma*F_2) for Gamma containing F_2
top5.argument: The only target found where the device does work the theorem cannot do: free products are functorial, so L(F_2)=L(F_3) yields Q*L(F_2)=Q*L(F_3) but not Q*L(Z)=Q*L(F_2). Every ingredient (free prefix family, a cocycle supported on the moved generator, a flow fixing a free factor, Nielsen correction, Baire generation) seems to transfer verbatim, and the Lean already has the fixed-generator variant (FiniteActive). Without the item a prover has no visible route; with it the proof is a re-parametrization. This is the cleanest jump test, but first check Dykema-Radulescu (2000) to make sure it is not already known.
top5.note_2026_10_10: Literature check (searches only; full texts of Dykema-Radulescu could not be fetched). (a) Not known before 287: for Gamma = F_2 the target reads L(F_3) = L(F_4), which is the free group factor problem itself (Dykema 1994 / Radulescu 1994 dichotomy), and no source found states L(Gamma*Z) = L(Gamma*F_2) for any Gamma whose factor is not an interpolated free group factor. (b) Dykema-Radulescu, Math. Ann. 316 (2000), arXiv math/9911011: for a II_1 factor N and A in the class F, N*A = N*L(F_r) with r = fdim(A). This preserves free dimension, so it does not give Q*L(Z) = Q*L(F_2). (c) RISK: Dykema-Radulescu, Proc. AMS 131 (2003), arXiv math/0105114, define Q(1)*...*Q(n)*L(F_r) for real r (negative allowed) by rescaling, with (Q*L(F_r))_t = Q_t*L(F_{t^-2 r}) for r>1 and small t, and give 'two statements equivalent to isomorphism of free group factors' (exact wording not retrieved). My own inference, unverified: with 287's theorem this rescaling formula gives Q*L(F_r) = Q*L(F_s) for every II_1 factor Q and r,s>1, and if the extended notation is consistent down to r=1 (L(F_1)=L(Z)), also Q*L(Z) = Q*L(F_2). In that case the target, for ICC Gamma, is a corollary of the theorem plus classical machinery, not reuse of the device, and the argument above ('functoriality does not give it') fails. Rank kept at 1 because this is not confirmed, but read math/0105114 before running the test; if confirmed, move it to theorem_corollaries (only non-factor L(Gamma) would remain a candidate) and promote smallCocycleTwo.

top5.title: smallCocycleTwo (rank-two small cocycle)
top5.lean: statable now; 1,808-line formal proof to compare
top5.argument: Most measurable: an existing Lean proof of a different statement that reuses the Radial shells. A prover given smallCocycle plus exists_small_prefix_inverse should need only the near-freeness counting. It is in-family, so it calibrates the harness rather than confirming a jump.

top5.title: Akemann-Ostrand lower bound via shells
top5.argument: A clean classical theorem (1976) whose lower bound follows from the Lean's shell recursion. It tests infrastructure reuse (the N0 radial calculus). Running it beside target 1 separates 'the item helped' from 'the shell library helped'.

top5.title: Fuchsian groups with torsion (de la Harpe-Voiculescu)
top5.argument: A genuine open problem with the same obstruction (beta_1^(2)>0, absorb generators) but relations break the one-generator cocycle. High payoff, low confidence; a good stretch target for the open-problem arm.

top5.title: 296's perturbation proposition
top5.argument: Release sibling with the same first-order structure. Expected speedup is low because the hard part is the nonlinear remainder, but it directly measures whether the cocycle viewpoint transfers within the release.

update_2026_10_10_web.shlyakhtenko_2609_11074: Direct fetch of arxiv.org/abs/2609.11074 failed (DNS / proxy 403). Search summaries of the abs page: D. Shlyakhtenko, 'On the II_1 Factors of Fuchsian Groups', math.OA, submitted 10 Sep 2026. Abstract: surface-group factors (genus g>=2) are free group factors on 2g-1 generators; key step is that the commutator ABA^-1B^-1 is freely complemented in L(F_2); together with earlier results this gives the de la Harpe-Voiculescu conjecture for finitely generated torsion-free non-elementary discrete subgroups of PSL_2(R); obtained using ChatGPT Pro 6.0. One summary instead says the paper cannot settle the conjecture in all cases and proves a weaker containment; that conflict was not resolved. Date and content agree with novelty.json; no cocycle with a prescribed value appears in what was seen.
earlier_equivalents: No earlier equivalent of the statement (a small-norm cocycle on one generator with D_w close to delta_e) was found. Closest neighbours: Pytlik-Szwarc / Szwarc deformations of the left regular representation of F_k and their l2 1-cocycles (arXiv 2607.17670, Jul 2026), Haagerup's tree cocycle, and Connes-Shlyakhtenko / Shlyakhtenko derivation-cocycle theory linking beta_1^(2), delta* and free entropy dimension. None prescribes a value at a word.

Free absorption L(Gamma*Z) = L(Gamma*F_2): see top5[0].note_2026_10_10. It was not known before 287 (for Gamma=F_2 it is the problem itself). Dykema-Radulescu 2003 rescaling may make it a corollary of the theorem for factor L(Gamma); this is unverified.
update_2026_10_10_web.u_n_plus: First L2-Betti number of the dual of U_N^+ is 1 (Vergnioux's conjecture, proved by Kyed-Raum; Bichon-Kyed-Raum, Math. Ann. 2018), and the higher ones vanish. Brannan-Vergnioux (arXiv 1703.08134) prove that orthogonal free quantum group factors are strongly 1-bounded. No source says whether L^infty(U_N^+) is a free group factor, so the open-problem row stands.
update_2026_10_10_web.net: No downgrade. No earlier equivalent of the statement; no post-release reuse; no error report. The post-release check is now weakly negative rather than inconclusive, limited by four days of coverage and by unreadable full texts.
